analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: Markets stumbled on the first day of Q4 with financial stress focused on Europe. The Franco-German 10yr spread rose 13.9bps, its biggest daily jump since March 2020, and the Italy-Bund 10yr spread rose 15.9bps, its biggest daily jump since July 2022. Sovereign contagion was a major talking point.

The moves had no single catalyst. The session began with a global bond selloff on higher oil prices and hawkish US data, with the US 10yr yield hitting 5.34% intraday, its highest since 2002. It then turned into risk-off, with Bunds and Treasuries rallying while French OATs and Italian BTPs sold off.

European risk assets and credit were hit. The CAC 40 (-1.62%) hit a 6-month low and the FTSE MIB (-2.21%) a 3-month low. STOXX Banks fell 3.90%, its worst day since March, with SocGen -5.00%, Credit Agricole -3.70% and BNP Paribas -3.64%. European HY spreads widened 18bps, the worst session since the start of the Iran war and the widest level in six months.
The euro fell 0.76% against the dollar, its worst day since June.

ECB pricing shifted dovish on the stress. Further hikes priced by December fell 6.1bps to 23.5bps, so another ECB hike is no longer fully priced by year-end. The 2yr German yield fell 14.2bps to 3.07%, its biggest drop since April, and the 10yr Bund yield fell 7.8bps to 3.51%.

Energy prices added pressure on Europe, an energy importer. Brent rose 4.37% to $102.31/bbl at the close and European natural gas futures rose 2.18%. Trump said in a Time interview it was 'possible' he would resume bombing Iran after the midterms, and Bloomberg reported the US was sending an additional aircraft carrier with 10,000 sailors and Marines to the Persian Gulf. There is no progress toward a deal and little sign that free shipping through the Strait of Hormuz resumes soon. The June 2027 Brent future hit a new high of $88.03/bbl.
The US diverged from Europe. The 10yr Treasury yield reversed to close down 4.4bps at 5.24%, and the S&P 500 (+0.19%) ended three straight declines. Futures are up another 0.27% this morning.

Dovish Fed commentary supported US markets. Vice Chair Jefferson said deciding on future hikes 'may take more time', and Governor Bowman said she did not 'currently see an urgent need for further action'. An October Fed hike was 30% priced at the close, down from 37% on Wednesday and 70% on Monday, before NY Fed President Williams signalled no urgency. The 2yr Treasury yield fell 9.6bps to 4.79%, its biggest daily decline since July.

US data was hawkish and showed resilience with price pressure. Initial jobless claims fell to a 10-week low of 197k (vs 200k expected) and continuing claims fell to a three-and-a-half-year low of 1.701m (vs 1.725m expected). ISM manufacturing was 54.5 (vs 55.0 expected), with prices paid at 77.9 (vs 73.0 expected) and employment at 52.7 (vs 52.0 expected).

Today's focus is the September US jobs report at 13:30 London time. DB economists expect payrolls of +60k (consensus 90k, prior 162k) with unemployment steady at 4.1%. Data resilience has supported US risk assets and given the Fed room to start hiking.

Asia was weaker overnight. The Hang Seng fell 2.64% on return from holiday and the Nikkei fell 0.94% after Tokyo CPI came in hotter than expected: headline 2.7% (vs 2.5% expected) and core-core 3.0% (vs 2.5% expected), the fastest in over a year. KOSPI rose 0.26% and South Korea CPI eased to 2.9%, in line. Mainland China markets were closed for a holiday.
Day ahead: US September jobs report and Euro Area flash CPI for September. Central bank speakers are the Fed's Logan and the ECB's Moulin, Cipollone, Rehn, Sleijpen, Vujcic and Nagel.

Stress in European banks and credit, with financial conditions tightening.
Higher oil prices from the Iran conflict and the Strait of Hormuz disruption, which hit energy-importing Europe harder.
US 10yr yield at 5.24% after touching the highest intraday level since 2002.
Persistent US price pressure, shown by ISM prices paid at 77.9.
Today's US jobs report as a swing factor for Fed hike pricing and US risk assets.

tension_points.bull_case: The US held up, with the S&P 500 up 0.19% and the 10yr yield reversing lower, helped by dovish Fed commentary and resilient data such as 10-week-low jobless claims.
tension_points.bear_case: European financial stress, wider sovereign spreads, higher oil and a hawkish US data mix (ISM prices paid at 77.9) could spill into US risk assets.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A weak or strong September jobs report today, against DB's +60k forecast and 90k consensus, would shift Fed hike pricing.
